title: EXP-025 — Designer Launch Click Telemetry
objective: From a qualifying baseline containing exactly one retained Web Client and one retained original Web Designer, with no rendered modal covering the launch surface and no visible authentication/session-establishment challenge, demonstrate that supported pre-activation observation is armed for browser-context page lifecycle plus request/response activity and, where supported, page-level popup and console activity. Then perform exactly one native Playwright click on the EXP-009/R2/EXP-024-correlated semantic "Open designer in a new window" control. Immediately enumerate the controlled pages, keep all telemetry listeners armed for a fixed five seconds after click completion, then perform one final enumeration and capture the resulting telemetry and rendered state. Classify only what was observed; do not infer command execution or failure from click completion, page count, HTTP status, console silence, or absence of captured telemetry.

in_scope: Read EXP-024, EXP-024-R2 and EXP-009-R2 before action so the semantic launch control and prior browser outcomes are identified correctly
Read-only preflight enumeration of every controlled browser page/window with URL and title
Read-only verification that the Web Client has no rendered modal covering the launch surface and no visible authentication/session-establishment challenge
Read-only verification that the semantic "Open designer in a new window" control is visibly present/enabled before activation
Before activation, demonstrably arm supported browser-context page lifecycle and request/response observation; supplement with page-level popup and console observation where supported
Record a task-local telemetry baseline immediately before activation so post-click activity can be correlated to the decisive action
Exactly one native Playwright activation of the EXP-009/R2/EXP-024-correlated launch control
Immediate independent enumeration of controlled pages/windows after the click completes or errors
Keep telemetry observation continuously armed for exactly five seconds after click completion, with no second launch action during that interval
Perform one final controlled-page enumeration after the five-second telemetry window closes
Inspect any newly enumerated controlled page sufficiently to identify URL/title and whether it is a Designer surface
If a distinct new Designer renders the normal editing-scope dialog, select User and confirm it only as necessary to identify the new client; perform no Form work
Record decisive evidence under evidence/EXP-025/ with a concise distinction between point-in-time page state, lifecycle history, console/network telemetry, and unsupported inferences
out_of_scope: Creating, editing, saving, closing, reopening, regenerating or deleting any Form or component
Testing Caption, Description, Static Caption, Button Caption, No Colon or Form-variable behavior
FormSync, generated SQL, variable serialization or database persistence
Determining the root cause of any observed or absent launch activity
Testing alternate Designer-launch commands, Runtime Builder, direct Designer URLs or other launch routes
Changing browser popup settings, security settings or browser configuration
Proving absence of OS/browser processes or browser-chrome popup UI outside the controlled automation context
Proving authentication-session, application-session, IDO Runtime-session or Designer-backend identity
Promoting an additional-Designer procedure unless the documented rendered new-tab/window postcondition is actually observed

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not perform more than one Designer-launch activation
Do not retry or perform a corrected launch click after the single activation, regardless of outcome
Do not use an alternate launch control, route, direct URL, synthetic DOM activation, page-evaluated click or script-triggered click
Do not perform the launch click unless AC-3 instrumentation is demonstrably armed through supported Playwright/MCP observation; if it cannot be armed, stop blocked
Do not close, reload, replace or deliberately navigate either retained Web Client or retained Designer before or during the telemetry window

Do not authenticate, sign in, click Sign In/OK, reauthenticate, log out or restart the browser during this experiment; if a rendered authentication/session-establishment challenge prevents the qualifying baseline, stop blocked
Do not open a Form in the Web Client or deliberately perform any Form operation
Do not Save, Regenerate Form, unload global Form objects, change User Preferences or change editing scope on the retained Designer
Do not alter browser popup-blocker or security settings

Do not stop telemetry observation before five seconds have elapsed after click completion unless the automation tool itself fails; if observation fails, record the failure without another launch attempt
Do not treat the immediate or final enumeration as proof that no transient page or popup existed
Do not treat a final screenshot as proof that no transient reload, navigation, replacement or Form opening occurred
Do not treat HTTP success, lack of network traffic, console silence, completed Playwright click or unchanged page count as proof that the Mongoose launch command executed or failed
Do not widen recovery beyond one fresh snapshot and one corrected read-only inspection; if the qualifying state remains unresolved, stop blocked
prohibited_patterns: \b(direct url|navigate directly|synthetic click|javascript click|dom click|page evaluate)\b

acceptance_checks.description: Before activation, evidence records every controlled page/window with URL/title and shows the qualifying point-in-time baseline contains the retained Web Client and retained original Designer; the inspected Web Client has no rendered modal covering the launch surface and no visible authentication/session-establishment challenge.

Pre-click rendered/accessibility evidence identifies the semantic "Open designer in a new window" control as visibly present/enabled and records its experiment-specific correlation without treating its Ext ID, ordinal position or accessibility ref as a supported product contract.

Before any launch activation, the worker demonstrates through supported Playwright/MCP facilities that browser-context page lifecycle and request/response observation are armed, with page-level popup and console observation also armed where supported, and captures a task-local pre-click baseline. No synthetic page scripting, DOM-triggered activation or prohibited recovery technique may be used to create this instrumentation. If the required lifecycle plus console/network observation cannot be demonstrably armed, EXP-025 stops BLOCKED here and no launch click occurs.

Exactly one native Playwright click is attempted on the correlated launch control. Evidence records whether Playwright completed it without actionability/interception error or returned an error. No retry, corrected click, alternate route or second launch activation occurs.

Immediately after the single click, controlled pages/windows are independently enumerated and their URL/title identities recorded. This acceptance check states only which controlled pages are present at that enumeration instant; if the same two pages are present, it makes no claim about whether a transient page/popup lifecycle event occurred before enumeration.

All armed telemetry remains active continuously until exactly five seconds after click completion. Evidence preserves and orders any launch-correlated browser-context page creation/closure/navigation event, popup event where supported, console message/error and relevant request/response observed during that fixed window. If none is captured in a telemetry class, the record says only that no event of that captured class was observed during the five-second window; absence is not proof that no Mongoose/client/backend processing occurred.

After the fixed five-second telemetry window closes, one final controlled-page enumeration records which pages/windows are present at that instant. The final enumeration is explicitly kept separate from AC-6 lifecycle history: a page observed transiently by AC-6 may legitimately be absent from AC-7.

If and only if a distinct new Designer is enumerated and renders the normal editing-scope dialog, evidence shows User selected and the resulting rendered Designer identified by URL/title. Otherwise no editing-scope interaction is performed, and the record states only that no such dialog was observed in the inspected controlled pages.

Execution-history evidence records that the worker deliberately performed no prohibited Form operation, retained-client close/reload/navigation, authentication action, preference change, unload, Save/Regenerate action, browser-setting change or second launch attempt. Separately, lifecycle/navigation telemetry reports whether any corresponding observable browser event occurred without intentional worker action. Final screenshots/enumeration are used only to establish final visible state, not historical absence of transient events.

Final evidence records the visible state of the retained controlled clients and repository confinement. Repository changes must be limited to the EXP-025 experiment record and evidence/EXP-025/. The final classification distinguishes point-in-time enumeration from lifecycle/console/network telemetry and makes no claim beyond those captured evidence classes.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261006-160452-YWtc. Rationale: EXP-024 and accepted clean replay EXP-024-R2 both reached the same narrow browser observation: after the launch surface appeared unobstructed, one Playwright click on the correlated "Open designer in a new window" control completed without the EXP-023 interception failure, yet immediate controlled-page enumeration still contained the retained Web Client and original Designer. The smallest useful next step is therefore not another lifecycle workaround but instrumentation of that single launch boundary. EXP-025 will arm supported browser-context lifecycle/network observation, supplemented by page-level popup/console observation where available, before exactly one launch click and keep it armed through a fixed five-second post-click observation window. Immediate and final page enumerations are treated only as point-in-time state observations; transient page/popup events are classified separately from the armed telemetry. If the required observation cannot be demonstrably armed through supported Playwright/MCP capabilities without synthetic scripting or prohibited techniques, the experiment stops blocked before any launch click.
